first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding is the most direct response to the current funnel deterioration and may improve time-to-value without conceding price. Verify the prior onboarding and signup experiments before committing, while guarding against lower-quality signups or downstream revenue dilution.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding-shortening experiment, prioritizing the confirmed improvement in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. This directly addresses the 4% completion decline and should support activation without sacrificing price or attracting lower-value accounts. Use activation, qualified revenue, and retention guardrails because signup simplification improved SMB activation but reduced 30-day retention by 1% and increased qualified revenue only 4%.

final2.rationale: The competitor’s deeper SMB price cut and doubled churn conversations create an immediate, segment-specific threat. A tightly targeted promotional-pricing test is the most direct response, supported by prior evidence of strong SMB acquisition and revenue lift. Keep it guarded with eligibility limits, duration and margin floors, and monitor qualified revenue, retention, and post-promotion churn to avoid trading sustainable revenue for temporary volume.
